brief: Goldman Sachs (John Flood, FICC & Equities) argues corporates remain the most consistent buyer of US equities, with demand accelerating rather than slowing despite investor fears that exploding hyperscaler capex would crimp corporate buybacks. Buyback growth from AI infrastructure stocks has more than offset the hyperscaler buyback decline, and GS expects total US corporate buybacks to rise to $1.7 trillion in 2027 from $1.5 trillion in 2026, citing NVDA's buyback authorization increase of $150 billion to $235 billion as an example. Growing cash M&A adds further equity demand. S&P 500 gross buybacks grew 15% y/y in H1 2026 and YTD buyback authorizations of $1.1 trillion run over 20% above last year. Flood combines this with GS's negative investor-sentiment indicator, light hedge fund net exposure, potential supercap IPOs exciting retail investors, and Q3 2026 consensus S&P 500 EPS growth of 27% y/y to conclude the market has 'the perfect recipe' for the S&P 500 to pierce 8,000 'in short order' as earnings season begins.
